top_categories.workout_context: 90ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Peaks Challenge Falls Creek, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
At mile 60 of 146, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
13,123ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Peaks Challenge Falls Creek's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before March.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Peaks Challenge Falls Creek. Train it until it feels boring.
13,123ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.

Road-specific control matters at Peaks Challenge Falls Creek. Practice on paved alpine roads through Victorian High Country: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 146 miles.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 146 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 13,123ft of climbing on paved alpine roads through Victorian High Country does to your power file on race day.
Low-cadence force work supports 13,123ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
146 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Peaks Challenge Falls Creek’s 146 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Moderate altitude at Peaks Challenge Falls Creek. Arrive 2–3 days early. Reduce intensity expectations by 5–10%. Hydrate aggressively.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Over Under, and Durability to prepare you for 146 miles of paved alpine roads through victorian high country in Falls Creek, Victoria, Australia.
